# SK2050 — Integer division feeds a fractional result

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A division evaluated in an integral type is converted to float, double or decimal, so the fractional part is discarded before the conversion that asks for it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, review it |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| ReSharper | `PossibleLossOfFraction` (`resharper_possible_loss_of_fraction_highlighting`) |

## Why

Asking for a fractional type is the author saying the fraction matters, and integral division has already thrown it away by the time the conversion runs. The truncation happens inside the operator, not at the assignment, so nothing in the surrounding code shows it. ⚠ The finding is independent of the checked context: no overflow is involved and the result is the same whether the project sets CheckForOverflowUnderflow or not. The fix casts the dividend to the fractional type, which changes the computed value — that is the point, and it is why the fix is not safe to apply unreviewed.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
double ratio = hits / total;
```

Write:

```csharp
double ratio = (double)hits / total;
```

## When it does not fire

Only built-in, non-lifted division whose result type is a fixed-width integral type is considered, and only where the result reaches float, double or decimal — either by conversion or through a cast written immediately around the division. ⚠ Roslyn does not report a cast's target as the operand's converted type, so `(double)(a / b)` is invisible to the conversion test and is matched by reading the enclosing cast instead; a rule that checked only the conversion would miss the commonest wrong repair for this defect while looking complete. ⚠ An explicit cast of the division to an *integral* type — `(long)(a / b)` in a double context — is read as the author saying truncation is intended, and is not reported; it is the documented way to keep the shape and silence the rule. Division by a constant 1 or -1, and a constant zero dividend, are exact and are not reported: the shape is present and no fraction is lost. Native integers, nullable operands, user-defined operators, dynamic and generic type parameters are excluded. The rule does not decide whether truncation was wrong, only that it happened before a fractional type was asked for.
